Description: This capability delta represents the gap between the current state and target state of Artificial Intelligence adoption and maturity across the enterprise. Closing this delta involves implementing AI technologies such as machine learning, natural language processing, and computer vision to automate processes, enhance decision-making, and drive innovation. Key focus areas include building scalable AI infrastructure, establishing data governance frameworks, and developing in-house AI expertise. Bridging this gap enables the enterprise to unlock competitive advantages through intelligent automation and data-driven insights.

This technical capability encompasses the use of AI-driven models and algorithms to autonomously produce written, visual, audio, or multimedia content. Leveraging large language models, generative adversarial networks, and other AI frameworks, the capability supports use cases such as automated report generation, marketing copy, code synthesis, and media creation. Integration with enterprise content management systems ensures generated outputs align with organizational standards, brand guidelines, and compliance requirements. Quality controls, including human-in-the-loop review processes, are applied to validate accuracy and appropriateness of generated content.

This technical capability encompasses the use of AI-driven tools and models to automatically generate source code based on natural language prompts, specifications, or existing code patterns. Leveraging large language models \(LLMs\), the capability accelerates software development by producing boilerplate code, unit tests, algorithms, and complete functions across multiple programming languages. Integration with developer toolchains, IDEs, and CI/CD pipelines enables seamless adoption into existing workflows. Governance controls, code quality validation, and security scanning are essential components to ensure generated code meets enterprise standards.

This technical capability encompasses the use of AI-driven models and algorithms to synthesize, generate, and manipulate images and video content from inputs such as text prompts, sketches, or existing media. Leveraging generative architectures such as GANs, diffusion models, and transformer-based systems, this capability enables the creation of photorealistic visuals, animations, and synthetic media at scale. Core use cases include content creation, data augmentation for ML pipelines, digital marketing assets, and simulation environments. Governance controls, including watermarking and provenance tracking, are essential to ensure responsible and compliant use across the enterprise.

This technical capability enables the automated generation of coherent, contextually relevant text using AI models such as large language models \(LLMs\). Applications include content creation, summarization, translation, code generation, and conversational interfaces. Underlying technologies typically leverage transformer-based architectures trained on large corpora to produce human-quality output across diverse domains and formats. Integration with enterprise systems allows for scalable, on-demand text generation to support business processes and customer-facing applications.

This technical capability addresses the gap between current and target-state competencies in human-AI interaction design and embodied AI systems. The delta encompasses conversational interfaces, multimodal interaction patterns, and the deployment of AI in physical or virtual embodied agents. Closing this gap requires investment in natural language processing, gesture and context-aware systems, and integration frameworks for robotics or avatar-based AI. Achieving target maturity enables more intuitive, natural, and effective engagement between users and AI-powered systems across enterprise touchpoints.

This technical capability encompasses the design, development, and deployment of AI-driven conversational interfaces, including chatbots, virtual assistants, and dialogue management systems. Conversation Systems leverage natural language processing \(NLP\) and machine learning models to interpret user intent, manage context, and generate coherent, contextually relevant responses. Integration with enterprise backend systems enables task automation, information retrieval, and transactional interactions across multiple channels such as web, mobile, and voice platforms. Key components include intent recognition, entity extraction, dialogue flow management, and continuous model training to improve accuracy and user experience over time.

This technical capability encompasses the design, development, and evaluation of interfaces and systems that enable effective interaction between humans and computers. It covers methodologies such as user experience \(UX\) design, natural language processing, gesture recognition, and multimodal interaction paradigms. The capability ensures that systems are intuitive, accessible, and optimized for human cognitive and physical capabilities. Application spans across AI-driven interfaces, conversational agents, adaptive systems, and intelligent assistive technologies.

This technical capability encompasses the design, development, and deployment of robotic systems that automate physical tasks through a combination of hardware, software, and AI-driven decision-making. Robotics integrates computer vision, motion planning, sensor fusion, and machine learning to enable autonomous or semi-autonomous operation in structured and unstructured environments. Applications span industrial automation, logistics, inspection, and human-robot collaboration scenarios. Effective implementation requires integration with enterprise systems, adherence to safety standards, and robust monitoring frameworks to ensure operational reliability.

This technical capability encompasses the ability of AI systems to interpret and comprehend data from various input modalities, including text, images, audio, and video. Perception and Understanding enables AI models to extract meaningful patterns, context, and semantics from raw data inputs, forming the foundation for downstream reasoning and decision-making. Core techniques include computer vision, natural language processing, speech recognition, and multimodal fusion. This capability is critical for building intelligent systems that can interact with and respond to real-world environments effectively.

This technical capability encompasses the processing, analysis, and transformation of audio signals and spoken language using AI and machine learning techniques. Core functions include automatic speech recognition \(ASR\), text-to-speech synthesis \(TTS\), speaker identification, sentiment analysis from voice, and noise reduction. The capability enables applications such as voice assistants, call center automation, real-time transcription, and audio content classification. Implementation relies on deep learning models, including transformer-based architectures, trained on large-scale multilingual audio datasets.

This technical capability enables automated extraction and interpretation of meaningful information from digital images, videos, and visual data streams. Computer Vision leverages machine learning models, including convolutional neural networks \(CNNs\) and transformer architectures, to perform tasks such as object detection, image classification, facial recognition, and scene understanding. Applications span quality control, surveillance, autonomous systems, and document processing. Integration with enterprise workflows enables real-time visual analytics and decision support at scale.

Natural Language Understanding \(NLU\) is a technical capability enabling systems to interpret, analyze, and derive meaning from human language input. This capability encompasses tasks such as intent recognition, entity extraction, sentiment analysis, and semantic parsing. NLU powers intelligent applications including conversational agents, document classification, and automated content analysis. Typically implemented via machine learning models and transformer-based architectures, this capability forms a foundational layer in AI-driven enterprise solutions.

This technical capability encompasses the methods and tools used to formally encode domain knowledge in machine-readable structures, enabling automated reasoning and inference. Supported techniques include ontologies, semantic networks, rule-based systems, and logic frameworks such as description logic and first-order logic. The capability underpins intelligent systems that derive conclusions, validate consistency, and answer complex queries based on structured knowledge bases. Applications span across decision support, natural language understanding, expert systems, and AI-driven automation initiatives.

This technical capability encompasses the mechanisms and processes by which AI systems acquire, refine, and generalise knowledge from data, experience, or feedback. Core techniques include supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning, enabling models to improve performance over time without explicit reprogramming. This capability underpins adaptive AI solutions that can respond to evolving data patterns and operational environments. Robust learning pipelines require quality training data, feature engineering, model validation, and continuous monitoring to ensure accuracy and reliability.

This technical capability encompasses AI-driven methods and algorithms used to automate and enhance complex planning and optimization processes across enterprise operations. Leveraging techniques such as mathematical programming, heuristic search, and reinforcement learning, this capability enables efficient allocation of resources, scheduling, and decision-making under constraints. Applications span supply chain optimization, workforce planning, route optimization, and capacity management. The capability delivers measurable improvements in operational efficiency, cost reduction, and throughput by identifying optimal or near-optimal solutions at scale.

Trend Forecasting is an AI-driven technical capability that applies machine learning models, statistical algorithms, and predictive analytics to analyze historical and real-time data, identifying patterns to predict future trends across business domains. This capability generates actionable forward-looking insights applicable to demand forecasting, market trend analysis, and operational performance prediction. Seamless integration with enterprise data pipelines enables continuous model refinement, ensuring sustained forecast accuracy and relevance. Governed model management and explainability features support enterprise-grade deployment and stakeholder trust.

Applied AI encompasses the practical deployment of artificial intelligence technologies to solve real-world business problems and automate decision-making processes. This capability covers the end-to-end lifecycle of AI solutions, from model development and training to production deployment and monitoring. Applied AI bridges the gap between theoretical AI research and tangible business value, enabling data-driven insights, predictive analytics, and intelligent automation across enterprise functions. Key focus areas include machine learning, natural language processing, computer vision, and AI-powered optimization of business processes.

This technical capability encompasses the design, development, and deployment of autonomous AI agents capable of perceiving their environment, making decisions, and executing actions to achieve defined objectives. AI agents leverage large language models, planning algorithms, and tool-use frameworks to perform complex, multi-step tasks with minimal human intervention. The capability includes orchestration of single and multi-agent architectures, memory management, and integration with external systems and APIs. Key enablers include robust monitoring, guardrails, and governance frameworks to ensure reliable, secure, and auditable agent behavior in enterprise contexts.

This technical capability encompasses the infrastructure, tools, and frameworks required to develop, train, deploy, and manage artificial intelligence and machine learning models at enterprise scale. AI Platforms provide end-to-end support for the full AI lifecycle, including data ingestion, feature engineering, model training, validation, and inference serving. Standardized platform services ensure governance, scalability, and reproducibility across AI initiatives, enabling consistent and auditable model management. Key components typically include MLOps tooling, compute orchestration, model registries, and monitoring capabilities to sustain production-grade AI solutions.

This capability delta represents the gap between current AI capabilities and the target state of deploying domain-specific AI solutions tailored to particular business verticals or functional areas. Closing this delta requires investment in specialised training data, fine-tuned models, and domain-expert collaboration to build AI systems that outperform general-purpose models within targeted domains. Key focus areas include industry-specific natural language processing, computer vision, and predictive analytics applications. Addressing this delta enables higher accuracy, relevance, and business value from AI deployments across specialised enterprise functions.

This technical capability encompasses the use of machine learning models capable of generating new content, including text, images, audio, and structured data, based on patterns learned from training data. Generative AI leverages architectures such as large language models \(LLMs\), diffusion models, and generative adversarial networks \(GANs\) to produce contextually relevant and novel outputs. Enterprise applications include automated content generation, code synthesis, data augmentation, and intelligent virtual assistants. Governance frameworks, including responsible AI policies and output validation mechanisms, are essential to ensure accuracy, compliance, and ethical use of generated content.

Diffusion Models are a class of generative AI models that learn to produce high-quality data outputs, such as images, audio, or video, by iteratively reversing a noise-addition process. During training, the model learns to denoise progressively corrupted data samples; during inference, new data is synthesized by starting from pure noise and applying learned denoising steps. This capability underpins state-of-the-art generative applications, including text-to-image synthesis, video generation, and molecular design. Key enterprise use cases include creative content generation, data augmentation, and simulation of complex systems.

This technical capability encompasses the development, deployment, and operationalization of large-scale neural language models trained on extensive text corpora to perform a wide range of natural language processing tasks. Capabilities include text generation, summarization, translation, semantic search, classification, and conversational AI, enabling automation of complex language-driven workflows. Integration with enterprise systems is achieved via API-based access patterns, supporting embedding within applications, services, and data pipelines. Governance considerations include model selection, fine-tuning strategies, prompt engineering standards, cost management, and responsible AI guardrails to ensure compliant and reliable usage.

This technical capability encompasses the design, development, and deployment of AI models capable of processing and integrating multiple data modalities, such as text, images, audio, and video, within a unified architecture. Multimodal models enable cross-modal reasoning and inference, allowing enterprise systems to derive richer insights from heterogeneous data sources. Key applications include visual question answering, document understanding, and speech-to-text integration with natural language processing. Adoption of this capability supports advanced AI use cases requiring contextual understanding across diverse input types.

Small Language Models \(SLMs\) are compact AI language models designed to perform natural language processing tasks with significantly fewer parameters than large-scale counterparts. SLMs are optimized for deployment in resource-constrained environments, including edge devices, embedded systems, and on-premises infrastructure, where latency, privacy, or compute limitations are critical factors. Despite reduced model size, SLMs achieve competitive performance on domain-specific tasks through techniques such as knowledge distillation, quantization, and fine-tuning on targeted datasets. This capability enables cost-efficient, scalable AI integration across enterprise workloads without dependency on high-capacity cloud infrastructure.

This technical capability encompasses the design, development, and deployment of machine learning models and algorithms that enable systems to learn from data and improve performance over time without explicit programming. The capability covers the full ML lifecycle, including data preparation, feature engineering, model training, validation, and productionization. Supported techniques include supervised, unsupervised, and reinforcement learning, as well as deep learning and neural network architectures. Governance, monitoring, and retraining pipelines ensure model accuracy, fairness, and reliability in production environments.

Deep Learning is a technical capability encompassing the design, development, and deployment of neural network architectures with multiple layers to model complex patterns in large datasets. This capability enables automated feature extraction, reducing the need for manual feature engineering while achieving state-of-the-art performance across domains such as image recognition, natural language processing, and predictive analytics. Implementation relies on frameworks such as TensorFlow or PyTorch, and typically requires GPU-accelerated computing infrastructure for training at scale. Effective governance of this capability includes model versioning, performance monitoring, and bias mitigation to ensure reliable and ethical AI outcomes.

This technical capability encompasses the design, development, and deployment of reinforcement learning \(RL\) systems, where agents learn optimal decision-making strategies through iterative interaction with an environment. Reward signals guide the training process, enabling autonomous optimization of complex sequential tasks such as resource allocation, process automation, and adaptive control systems. Core competencies include policy optimization algorithms \(e.g., Q-learning, PPO, A3C\), environment simulation, and reward function engineering. Application domains span robotics, real-time bidding, recommendation engines, and enterprise process automation.

Supervised Learning is a machine learning technique in which algorithms are trained on labeled datasets to learn mappings between input features and known output values. The trained model generalizes from this labeled data to make accurate predictions or classifications on unseen inputs. Common applications include image recognition, natural language processing, fraud detection, and predictive analytics. Model performance is evaluated using metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score against held-out validation and test datasets.

Unsupervised Learning is a machine learning technique that enables systems to identify patterns, structures, and relationships within unlabeled datasets without explicit guidance or predefined outputs. Common applications include clustering, dimensionality reduction, and anomaly detection, supporting use cases such as customer segmentation, fraud detection, and data compression. Algorithms such as k-means, DBSCAN, autoencoders, and principal component analysis \(PCA\) are foundational to this capability. Unsupervised Learning is critical for extracting actionable insights from large, unstructured datasets where manual labeling is impractical or cost-prohibitive.

Technology Platforms and Enterprise Information Assets which combine to enable an accurate, relevant, timely and consistent measure of organisational performance, as well as the development of new and competitive understanding of both market and customers behaviour as well as the organization's own operations.

Description: The ability to aggregate data as the basis for performance measurement, for example via Key Performance Indicators, and insight into customer behaviour, market trends, propositional and operational performance.

The ability to mine structured and unstructured data to identify patterns and establish relationships; extrapolate historical data to predict the future using “what-if” scenarios to support decision making and planning. Analytics can take place 'offline' i.e. on historical data, or 'real-time' i.e. whilst a business or system transation is still in flight.

Application/Technology Service: Power BI desktop (pro),Jaggaer (Bravo Spend Analytics),PowerBI 365,Salesforce Tableau
Description: The ability to aggregate data as the basis for performance measurement, for example via Key Performance Indicators, and insight into customer behaviour, market trends, propositional and operational performance.

The ability to capture, store and make available as the basis for reporting and analysis, business and technical data, most commonly structured or semi-structured, but not excluding unstructured content.

The ability to store, and query ‘big data’ (often characterised by the "3 Vs": variety, velocity  and volume) whose structrue, volume and rate of change makes the use of traditional data management technologies (e.g. RDBMS) impractical or uneconomic.

Enables the storage of data, including history, from disparate sources in a consistent, integrated fashion. Includes the capability to store very large amounts of data, usually captured from other database systems and to perform on-line analytical processing on it in support of ad-hoc queries.

The ability to provision the computing and network resources required by the organization, either through direct ownership of datacentre and network resources, or through their consumption via a Third Party service.
The ability to run one or more applications on physical or virtual servers.

Application Virtualization (also known as Process Virtualization) is software technology that encapsulates computer programs from the underlying operating system on which it is executed. A fully virtualized application is not installed in the traditional sense, although it is still executed as if it were. The application behaves at runtime like it is directly interfacing with the original operating system and all the resources managed by it, but can be isolated or sandboxed to varying degrees.

A database is a structured collection of data. The data are typically organized to model relevant aspects of reality (for example, the availability of rooms in hotels), in a way that supports processes requiring this information (for example, finding a hotel with vacancies).
File transfer is a generic term for the act of transmitting files over a computer network. There are numerous ways and protocols to transfer files over a network (e.g. FTP).

The ability to run one or more applications through the provisioning of a physical or virtual server as well as its operating system and associated functions, such as a run-time container and job scheduling utilities.

Server virtualisation is a virtualisation technique that involves partitioning a physical server into a number of small, virtual servers with the help of virtualisation software. In server virtualisation, each virtual server runs multiple operating system instances at the same time.

This technical capability encompasses the tools, and processes required to migrate, deploy, and operate workloads across public, private, or hybrid cloud environments. Cloud Enablement includes infrastructure provisioning, cloud-native architecture adoption, security and compliance enforcement, and cost optimization practices. The capability supports scalability, resilience, and agility by leveraging cloud service models such as IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS. Foundational to digital transformation, this capability ensures consistent governance and operational standards across all cloud platforms.

A cloud broker is a third-party individual or business that acts as an intermediary between the purchaser of a cloud computing service and the sellers of that service. In general, a broker is someone who acts as an intermediary between two or more parties during negotiations.

This technical capability encompasses the tools, processes, and governance frameworks required to provision, monitor, optimize, and secure cloud resources across public, private, and hybrid cloud environments. Cloud Management includes capacity planning, cost optimization, performance monitoring, and policy enforcement to ensure efficient utilization of cloud infrastructure. The capability supports multi-cloud strategies by providing centralized visibility and control over workloads, services, and data assets. Automation and orchestration are key enablers, reducing operational overhead and ensuring consistent compliance with enterprise standards.

This technical capability enables the packaging and deployment of applications within lightweight, isolated containers that bundle all required dependencies, libraries, and configurations. Containerisation ensures consistent runtime environments across development, testing, and production, reducing infrastructure complexity and eliminating environment-specific defects. The capability supports scalable microservices architectures, rapid deployment cycles, and efficient resource utilisation by sharing the host OS kernel. Orchestration platforms such as Kubernetes complement this capability by managing container lifecycle, scaling, and resilience at enterprise scale.
The configuration, monitoring, administration, accounting and workload management of IT Infrastructure.
Ability to perform administration on the IT Infrastructure assets
Ability to monitor how well our IT Infrastructure assets are running, and proactively identify problems
Ability to make the most efficient use of the available IT Infrastructure assets in support of IT service demand and priorities.

Technologies and Services to deliver a consistent, business enabling global voice and data network for the organization that uses industry standards and delivers scalable services through implementation of a common architecture with agreed technologies, standards and repeatable service patterns.

A network firewall protects a computer network from unauthorized access. It might take the form of a hardware device, a software program, or a combination of the two. Network firewalls guard an internal computer network against malicious access from the outside, such as malware-infested websites or vulnerable open network ports. You can find network firewalls in homes, schools, businesses, and intranets.

Network monitoring is a computer network's systematic effort to detect slow or failing network components, such as overloaded or crashed/frozen servers, failing routers, failed switches or other problematic devices. In the event of a network failure or similar outage, the network monitoring system alerts the network administrator.
The ability to support the running of one or more networks.

In computing, network virtualisation or network virtualisation is the process of combining hardware and software network resources and network functionality into a single, software-based administrative entity, a virtual network. Network virtualization involves platform virtualization, often combined with resource virtualisation.
The provisioning and management of the underlining infrastructure enabling the storage of information.
Block services addresses data by disk block number and transfers low level fixed size raw disk blocks on a storage device (disk or tape). It is accessed by the operating system and disk controllers.

A distributed file system (DFS) is a file system with data stored on a server. The data is accessed and processed as if it was stored on the local client machine. The DFS makes it convenient to share information and files among users on a network in a controlled and authorized way.

Object based services addresses the encapsulation of data and its unique set of attributes, with object-based access, data that is stored via unique address identifiers is read and write to actual storage as blocks of data.
Fixed content data repositories that have long-term value, that do not change over time, and are easily accessible.
Provide a multi-level storage facility to ensure data recovery to a consistent point in time, incl. Multi version point-in-time backups; Restore Services; Cataloguing and indexing.

Technologies Platforms which enable different IT systems to interoperate in order to deliver both seamless end-to-end processing; the integration of business information to provide a common view of business operations and performance; and the discovery and automation of business processes and business logic.

The ability to control and monitor message exchange between systems, resolve contentions, manage the deployment and versioning of services and support commodity services like event handling, event choreography and data transformation.

The process of creating and publishing web APIs, enforcing their usage policies, controlling access, nurturing the subscriber community, collecting and analyzing usage statistics, and reporting on performance. API Management components provide mechanisms and tools to support developer and subscriber community.

Real time, highly available, high performing integration of applications, data and platforms. The prime duties of an ESB are to: Monitor and control routing of message exchange between services; Resolve contention between communicating service components; Control deployment and versioning of services; Marshal use of redundant services; Cater for commonly needed commodity services like event handling and event choreography, data transformation and mapping, message and event queuing and sequencing, security or exception handling, protocol conversion and enforcing proper quality of communication service; Provide standard adapters for consistent connectivity to heterogeneous systems.

Application/Technology Service: IASME,Charities Commission Service,Postcode Search Facility,Spotlight,Contracts Finder Service,Find a Tender Service
Description: This technical capability encompasses the design, development, and management of externally exposed Application Programming Interfaces \(APIs\) that enable third-party systems, partners, and customers to integrate with enterprise services and data. The capability includes API lifecycle management, versioning, authentication, authorization, and rate limiting to ensure secure and reliable access. Governance frameworks and developer portals support onboarding, documentation, and consumption of APIs at scale. This capability is foundational for enabling ecosystem integration, digital partnerships, and platform extensibility.

The ability to integrate data between and across multiple systems, including the ability to map multiple inputs to a common schema or set of business definitions; the ability to reconcile multiple versions of the truth and establish an authoritative source; and the ability to understand data lineage and provenance, including transformation and derivation of individual data items.

Validate, cleanse, conform and transform data by gathering it together from similar sources to provide a single overarching view. Extract, Transform and Load (ETL) refers to a process in database usage and especially in data warehousing that involves: Extracting data from outside sources, Transforming it to fit operational needs (which can include quality levels) and Loading it into the end target (database, more specifically, operational data store, data mart or data warehouse).
MDM remove duplicates, standardises data (mass maintaining), and incorporates rules to eliminate incorrect data from entering the system in order to create an authoritative source of master data.

Metadata management involves managing metadata about other data, whereby this "other data" is generally referred to as content data. The term is used most often in relation to digital media, but older forms of metadata are catalogs, dictionaries, and taxonomies.

This technical capability encompasses the design, orchestration, and monitoring of automated pipelines used to manage the flow of data, code, or processes across systems. Pipeline management ensures reliable execution, sequencing, and error handling of tasks within CI/CD, data ingestion, or processing workflows. The capability includes tooling and governance to define pipeline configurations, track execution state, and enable scalable throughput. Operational observability, dependency management, and recovery mechanisms are integral components of this capability.

This technical capability encompasses the processes, tools, and frameworks used to convert data, structures, or systems from one format, model, or state to another. Transformation supports integration pipelines, data migration, and modernization initiatives by enabling seamless interoperability between disparate systems and technologies. Core activities include data mapping, format conversion, schema translation, and business rule application to ensure accuracy and consistency of transformed outputs.

{color:rgb(10, 10, 10)/}This relates to the discipline of creating and maintaining an organised inventory of an organisation's data assets, providing a searchable and centralised view of all its data, including databases, files, and reports.{color}

This relates to establishing a framework of rules, policies, standards, and processes that ensures an organisation's data is secure, accurate, and properly managed throughout its lifecycle. It establishes accountability and guides the collection, storage, and use of data to maximize its value, reduce risks, and meet compliance requirements like GDPR. Data governance includes defining roles like data owners and stewards, implementing quality checks, and ensuring the data is trustworthy and accessible to the right people. 

**Key components of data governance**

*   **Policies and procedures**: These are the official rules and guidelines for how data is handled across the organization.

*   **Roles and responsibilities**: Specific individuals or teams are assigned accountability for data, such as data owners and data stewards.

*   **Data quality**: It involves processes to ensure data is accurate, consistent, and reliable.

*   **Security and privacy**: This includes measures to protect sensitive data and comply with regulations such as HIPAA, GDPR, and CCPA.

*   **Data lifecycle management**: The framework covers data from its creation and collection to its storage, use, and eventual deletion.

*   **Technology and tools**: Data governance is supported by technology that helps implement policies, monitor compliance, and manage data.

Integration Middleware is a technical capability that enables seamless communication and data exchange between disparate applications, systems, and services across the enterprise landscape. This capability encompasses message brokering, API management, data transformation, and protocol mediation to ensure interoperability across heterogeneous environments. Integration Middleware supports both synchronous and asynchronous communication patterns, including event-driven architectures, to facilitate real-time and batch processing needs. This capability is foundational to enterprise-wide digital integration strategies, reducing point-to-point complexity and enabling scalable, maintainable system connectivity.
The automation of manual process and of business logic, as well as its discovery, analysis and ongoing monitoring.

The run time automated orchestration (control) of pre defined tasks for well defined and highly repeatable business processes. This includes services to support real time operational management (task assignment, (manual) task reallocation, tracking, notification and identity. checking) of end to end processes, workflow and pipeline.

A Business Rules Engine is a software system that executes one or more business rules in a runtime production environment. Rule engines typically support rules, facts, priority (score), mutual exclusion, preconditions, and other functions. Rule engine software is commonly provided as a service of Business Rules Management which, among other functions, provides the ability to: Register, define, classify, and manage all the rules and verify consistency of rules definitions.
Job scheduling software automates the process of managing and executing tasks or jobs on a schedule.

Process mining is a family of techniques in the field of process management that support the analysis of business processes based on event logs. During process mining, specialized data mining algorithms are applied to event log data in order to identify trends, patterns and details contained in event logs recorded by an information system. Process mining aims to improve process efficiency and understanding of processes.

Technologies that allow the build, deployment and operation of digital User Interfaces (UIs) allowing direct human-to-machine interaction. While most systems have some kind of UI, this especially applies to those that use digital technologies (e.g. Android OS) or internet standards and protocols (e.g. HTTPS) to allow user interaction across a range of computing devices. Also included in this component is the design and monitoring of user interfaces to create meaningful User Experiences (UX).

Capabilities required for the development and maintenance of websites or digtal applications, as well as for analysing their usage and confguring to their end-user's needs. Note that these capabilities are additional to the core software development capabilities covered in IT Development.

The means of managing any digital content used in the build, configuration, or population of a website or digital portal, including textual content, images, video, stying and branding rules etc. This will typically include management of their configuration and development/deployment/archiving lifecycle.
The ability to adapt the user experience to the needs or preferences of an individual, based on data held about them as well as their dynamic behavior.
Analysis of user interaction with an interface, for the purpose of optmising interface design and creating compelling user experiences.
Websites and web applications designed to expose content, information and function out to users over an internet connection or to be accessible via a mobile device.

This technical capability encompasses the creation, storage, distribution, and lifecycle management of digital brochures across the enterprise. It enables the production of rich, interactive digital marketing and informational materials, supporting multiple formats and channels for broad audience reach. The capability integrates with content management and digital asset management systems to ensure version control, brand consistency, and timely updates. Key functions include template management, multi-channel publishing, and analytics to measure brochure engagement and effectiveness.

This technical capability encompasses the design, development, hosting, and management of publicly accessible web presence serving external stakeholders such as customers, partners, and prospects. The capability includes content management, web performance optimization, security controls, and compliance with accessibility standards. Core functions cover domain management, SSL certificate handling, CDN integration, and analytics to monitor user engagement and site performance.

This technical capability encompasses the practices, tools, and processes required to optimize digital content and web properties for improved visibility in search engine results pages \(SERPs\). Activities include keyword research, on-page optimization, technical SEO auditing, link building, and performance monitoring. The capability enables data-driven decisions to enhance organic search rankings, drive targeted traffic, and improve overall digital presence. Key metrics include organic traffic volume, keyword rankings, crawl efficiency, and conversion rates from organic search channels.
A website or web application designed or optimised for mobile devices and potentially integrating with other mobile functions (e.g. location or mapping services).

An interface that allows the user to interact with the application via natural human language (e.g. speech or text input) rather than constraining them to a number of defined options or set interactions.

This technical capability enables the rapid creation and iterative development of service prototypes to validate concepts, test functionality, and gather stakeholder feedback before full-scale implementation. Service Prototyping provides tools, frameworks, and methodologies for building low to high-fidelity service models that demonstrate core features, user interactions, and integration points. The capability supports agile development practices by reducing time-to-market, minimizing development risks, and ensuring alignment between technical solutions and business requirements. Key outcomes include validated service designs, refined requirements, and improved stakeholder confidence in proposed solutions.

A website or digital portal consisting primarily of web content or unstructured data, for example, narrative text, images, video or audio. It may host this information natively, or be a means of accessing it (e.g. by dowloading documents), but is not capable of transaction processing, i.e. processing structured data in accordance with defined logic or algorithms.

Native web applications (i.e. that run in a browser). Although they will often have a server component, they differ from portals in that they are native web applications and not a web façade on an existing application (e.g. an on-premise ERP system).

A website or digital portal primarily designed for the capture and processing of structured data according to defined logic or algorithms. Web portals are not complete applications in themselves (i.e. consisting of a User Interface, Logic and Database layers) but are means of accessing data or exposing function from other applications.
The ability to efficiently design, build and deploy software across both waterfall and agile delivery models.

The ability to code applications, modules, services, utilities and any other component of an IT system, to analyse and test code for efficiency, compliance to standards and fit with business and user requirements, and to maintain those code artefacts through the development process.
Software applications that provides comprehensive facilities for the development of mobile applications and utilities.

This technical capability enables rapid application development through visual interfaces and declarative configuration rather than traditional hand-coded programming. The capability leverages platforms that provide pre-built components, drag-and-drop functionality, and automated code generation to accelerate delivery cycles and reduce dependency on specialized development resources. No-code solutions target business users with minimal technical expertise, while low-code platforms serve professional developers seeking to streamline routine development tasks. Key benefits include faster time-to-market, reduced development costs, improved business-IT collaboration, and increased organizational agility in responding to changing requirements.

Software configuration management \(SCM\) is a software engineering discipline consisting of standard processes and techniques often used by organizations to manage the changes introduced to its software products. SCM helps in identifying individual elements and configurations, tracking changes, and version selection, control, and baselining.

{color:rgb(0, 29, 53)/}AI testing encompasses two main areas: **testing of AI applications to ensure they function as intended, and the use of AI \(like machine learning and NLP\) to enhance and automate traditional software testing**. AI testing involves validating an AI's accuracy, reliability, and performance, while also leveraging AI capabilities to speed up test execution, predict defects, and reduce maintenance.{color}

API testing is a type of software testing that analyzes an application programming interface\(API\) to verify that it fulfills its expected functionality, security, performance and reliability. The tests are performed either directly on the API or as part of Integration testing. It is usually executed before the UI is available.

Accessibility testing assesses a digital product's compliance with accessibility standards. The goal is to make digital products inclusive and accessible to people with disabilities.  
It is achieved by checking Webpages for WCAG compliance, testing with accessibility tools such as screen readers, and conducting user testing.  
Uses free plug-ins Free plug-ins \(WAVE, AXE Core, Accessibility Insights\)

Canary Testing is a technical capability that enables controlled, incremental rollout of new software releases to a small subset of users or infrastructure before full deployment. This approach reduces deployment risk by validating changes in a production environment while limiting the blast radius of potential failures. Metrics and performance indicators are monitored during the canary phase to determine whether the release is stable enough for broader rollout. Automated rollback mechanisms are typically integrated to revert the canary deployment if anomalies or degradation are detected.

Cross Browser/Device is a type of non-functional testing that checks whether your website works as intended when accessed through  
Different Browser-OS combinations i.e., on popular browsers like Firefox, Chrome, Edge, Safari; and on popular operating systems like Windows, macOS, iOS and Android.  
Different devices i.e., users can view and interact with your website on popular devices—smartphones, tablets, desktops and laptops etc.

Non-functional testing evaluates the system’s performance, scalability, security, usability, and reliability, rather than its specific functionality. It ensures that the system can handle real-world demands and provides a seamless, high-quality user experience.

Performance testing is a type of non-functional testing. It measures how well the system performs under load conditions. Performance testing evaluating application output, processing speed, data transfer velocity, network bandwidth usage, maximum concurrent users, memory utilization, workload efficiency, and response times.
Automated testing is the implementation of an automation tool to execute test cases. The goal of automation is to provide faster, more consistent, repeatable, and more cost effective test results

Multi Factor Authentication \(MFA\) is a technical security capability that requires users to verify their identity through two or more independent authentication factors before gaining access to a system or application. These factors typically combine something the user knows \(password\), something the user possesses \(hardware token or mobile device\), and something the user is \(biometric data\). MFA significantly reduces the risk of unauthorised access resulting from compromised credentials. This capability is foundational to Zero Trust security architectures and is typically enforced across all critical enterprise systems and access points.

This technical capability covers the implementation and management of password-based authentication mechanisms to verify user identities and control access to systems and resources. Key aspects include password policy enforcement \(complexity, expiration, and reuse rules\), secure credential storage using hashing and salting techniques, and integration with identity management systems. Password Authentication serves as a foundational security control, ensuring that only authorised users gain access to enterprise applications and data.
